steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Depth Study (Paper 2) is worth 50% of the GCSE and lasts 1 hour 30 minutes

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: It focuses on a shorter period in much greater detail, requiring depth of knowledge and source analysis

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Source-based questions are central to the Depth Study — you must use sources as evidence

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The paper may ask you to evaluate the utility of a source for a specific question

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What percentage of the GCSE is the Depth Study worth? | Q: What is the key difference between the Period Study and the Depth Study? | Q: Why must you combine source evidence with your own knowledge?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 50% — it is Paper 2, equally weighted with the Period Study (Paper 1). | The Period Study covers a broad period focusing on narrative and causation; the Depth Study covers a shorter period in detail, emphasising source analysis and interpretations. | Because your own contextual knowledge allows you to evaluate the source's accuracy, identify what it omits, and provide a fuller analysis than the source alone can give.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: For source utility questions, use the structure: 'The source is useful for X because... However, it is limited for Y because...' When comparing interpretations, identify specific points of agreement AND disagreement, then explain why Always use contextual knowledge to test what a source says — does other evidence support or contradict it? In the extended question, structure your answer around 2-3 main arguments supported by both source evidence and your own knowledge Don't just describe what a source says — analyse its provenance, purpose and limitations
